understand.concept: itertools contains fast, memory-efficient iterator building blocks. Functions such as chain combine iterables, islice selects a portion, product generates Cartesian products and groupby groups adjacent equal keys. Some iterators such as count and cycle can be infinite, so consumers must apply a stopping condition.
understand.whyItMatters: itertools helps express common iteration patterns without writing repetitive loops or materializing large intermediate collections.
understand.analogy: itertools is a set of modular conveyor-belt connectors for combining and shaping streams of items.
understand.analogyLimit: Some tools produce infinite streams, and groupby groups consecutive runs rather than all equal keys globally; consuming or sorting data incorrectly can produce surprising results.
understand.summary: itertools for Efficient Iteration develops advanced Python programming skills.

explain.narrative:
## Compose iterator building blocks
`chain` yields values from multiple iterables in sequence. `islice` selects a range of values without materializing the full input. `product` generates Cartesian products. `repeat` repeats a value, and `count` can generate an unbounded sequence. `groupby` groups consecutive items sharing a key, so sort by that key first when global grouping is required.

Use these tools to make iteration intent clear. Be careful with infinite iterators: pass them to a bounded consumer or use islice to limit the number of values.

examples.title: Chain two iterables
examples.explanation: chain yields values from each input iterable in order.

examples.title: Take a bounded slice
examples.code:
from itertools import count, islice
print(list(islice(count(10), 4)))
examples.explanation: islice limits consumption of the infinite count iterator.

examples.title: Generate a Cartesian product
examples.explanation: product generates combinations across the input iterables.

examples.title: Repeat a value a fixed number of times
examples.explanation: repeat produces the same value the specified number of times.

examples.title: Group adjacent equal values
examples.code:
from itertools import groupby
values = [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3]
print([(key, len(list(group))) for key, group in groupby(values)])
examples.explanation: groupby groups consecutive runs with equal keys.
